title: A Transparent Power Ranking: Where Should Punjab Kings Stand and Why?
dek: Where should Punjab Kings stand right now? A power ranking built from two published numbers, net run rate and win rate, shows its working.
excerpt: Across 2025–2026, Punjab Kings rank second of ten on a transparent power ranking that blends how much they outscore opponents with how often they win. Every input is public and every step is shown.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

Across the ten franchises, net run rate and win rate correlate at {{ev:pr-r}}.

sections.heading: Rankings You Can Check
body: Most power rankings are opinions with numbers attached. This one uses two measures anyone can verify: net run rate, which captures how dominant a side is, and win rate, which captures results.
Each is standardised across the ten franchises and the two are averaged. Over 2025–2026, {{ev:pr-top}} rank first.

sections.heading: Where PBKS Stand
body: Punjab Kings rank {{ev:pr-me-rank}} of ten, with a net run rate of {{ev:pr-net}} runs an over and a win rate of {{ev:pr-win}}.
Across the league, the two inputs correlate at {{ev:pr-r}}: sides that outscore opponents usually win, but not always.

sections.heading: Why Two Inputs
body: Win rate alone rewards close-match luck; net run rate alone rewards thrashings of weak sides. Blending them balances both.

sections.heading: Limits
body: The ranking ignores strength of schedule and squad changes during the season. Two seasons of data smooth noise but react slowly to change.
Net run rate here is runs per over scored minus conceded, without the official adjustments for innings that end early.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Second on the Evidence
body: On recent evidence, Punjab Kings belong second in the league.
Adding strength of schedule is the obvious next refinement.
